text:
secops-bot: [ALERT] SSO anomaly detected \u2014 impossible-travel events for multiple identities. 3 lockouts, surge in MFA prompts. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sso-anomalies

alex_k: seeing the same. multiple lockouts in the last 12m, countries show CA -> DE -> IN for same user sessions.

maria_s: which accounts? can you paste the usernames?

alex_k: affected: jdoe@redwood.com, opsbot@redwood.com, ml-ci@redwood.com (partial list).

samir_p: recommend immediate containment: revoke all active sessions for the affected accounts, force password reset + require new MFA enrollment. pinging Okta SSO team. @maria_s can you help coordinate user comms? :rotating_light:

irene_t: MFA fatigue spike in telemetry too (auth.prompts.count +420% in 10m). could be automated credential stuffing or phishing.

alex_k: pulled Okta logs snippet:
```
2025-06-12T14:02:10Z okta.auth event=authentication user=jdoe method=sso ip=23.45.67.89 geo=CA result=SUCCESS
2025-06-12T14:07:22Z okta.auth event=authentication user=jdoe method=sso ip=5.6.7.8 geo=DE result=SUCCESS device=android
2025-06-12T14:11:01Z okta.auth event=authentication user=jdoe method=password ip=103.21.12.13 geo=IN result=FAILURE reason=invalid_credentials
2025-06-12T14:12:40Z okta.event event=session_lockout user=ml-ci reason=too_many_attempts
```

maria_s: running log query now: `okta logs search --from "-30m" --filter "result eq \"FAILURE\" or eventType eq \"user.session.lockout\""`

samir_p: I just pushed session revokes for the three accounts and created a denylist for the suspect IPs (23.45.67.89, 5.6.7.8, 103.21.12.13). Okta shows revocation succeeded.

alex_k: added temporary rate-limit on SSO endpoints for non-verified apps, turned on stricter device challenge for web flows.

irene_t: opening an incident now: INC-2025-042. assigning oncall security (samir_p). I'll attach evidence and initial impact.

maria_s: prepping user notification draft: short note, forced sign-out, steps to reset MFA, link to support. Will send after legal OK.

samir_p: quick note on next steps:
- finish root cause triage (are service accounts being abused?)
- check KMS access logs for any unusual key usage tied to these identities
- check audit logs for recent RBAC changes that could explain automated token refreshes
- keep session revokes in place until we validate

alex_k: I also triggered a rolling session-clear for all CI service tokens as a precaution. will post a postmortem checklist in the incident.

irene_t: agreed. once containment validated, we'll coordinate a company-wide status update and record lessons (auth throttles, alert tuning, runbook gaps). :white_check_mark:

secops-bot: [INFO] Incident INC-2025-042 created by irene_t. Current severity: P2 -> reviewing for escalation.

alex_k: thanks everyone. if you see any exec or legal asks escalate to me and irene.

maria_s: will follow up with draft and list of impacted users.

samir_p: monitoring for re-attempts; will update channel on any new lockouts or unusual IPs.
